papers.title: BixBench3: Benchmarking AI agents on research-study-scale computational biology tasks
papers.authors: Zane Koch, Asmamaw T. Wassie, Javier Valdes-Aleman, Jason Lee, Michaela M. Hinks, Samuel G. Rodriques, Andrew D. White, Jon M. Laurent
papers.summary: Benchmarks agents on 20 study-scale computational-biology tasks and 138 programmatically graded artifacts; the best of 13 frontier models scores 0.48.
papers.use: Directly matches Yoshitaka's agent-driven BioWulf analysis workflow.
papers.steal: Grade intermediate artifacts and stratify failures by data size and workflow depth.
papers.doubt: Artifact agreement is not scientific validity; how are multiple valid analyses handled?

papers.title: When Riemann flows with Wasserstein: Generative Modeling of Probability Distributions on Manifolds
papers.authors: Doron Haviv, Edward De Brouwer, Rishabh Anand, Rex Ying, Aïcha Bentaieb, Gabriele Scalia, Hector Corrada Bravo
papers.summary: Riemannian Wasserstein entropic flow matching generates distributions on manifolds, including whole single-cell samples and protein ensembles.
papers.use: A population-level alternative to mean-latent patient transitions.
papers.steal: Model conditional transitions between cell distributions and compare Euclidean versus manifold geometry.
papers.doubt: Does geometric fidelity improve treatment-response transfer, and is the chosen manifold justified?

papers.title: ArticleMiner: Ontology-Guided Knowledge Graph Construction from Scientific Publications
papers.authors: Md Abrar Jahin, Craig A. Knoblock, Jay Pujara
papers.summary: Combines paper and supplement parsers, LLM evidence, and bounded domain modules to emit constrained RDF facts across four scientific domains.
papers.use: A close design reference for extracting quantitative evidence into OncoGraph.
papers.steal: Retain parser provenance and promote facts only after task-specific validity checks.
papers.doubt: Can the drug-discovery module preserve conditions, negative results and contradictions?

papers.title: Beyond Natural Language: An Agent-Native Language for Autonomous Science
papers.summary: Lara encodes claims, evidence, assumptions and objections as machine-checkable programs with reproducible epistemic statuses.
papers.use: Points toward an auditable claim graph for OncoGraph.
papers.steal: Add explicit support, assumption, objection and gap states before answer generation.
papers.doubt: Formal consistency cannot verify empirical truth, and manual encoding may be costly.

papers.title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
papers.authors: Dhruv Srikanth, Bingchen Zhao, Dixing Xu, Yuxiang Wu, Zhengyao Jiang
papers.summary: AIDE² iteratively rewrites and selects its own research-agent code, finding seven improvements that transfer to held-out task families.
papers.use: Directly relevant to Yoshitaka's self-improving research automation.
papers.steal: Version each accepted change and jointly track hidden transfer, reward hacking and cost.
papers.doubt: Can hidden tests prevent evaluation-infrastructure gaming, and is the eight-day run reproducible?

papers.title: Entropy Can Flow, or It Can Guide. Be Entropy. LEDFlow: Introducing Entropy-guided Generation Order into Uniform Discrete Flow
papers.authors: Tung Sum Thomas Kwok, Yidong Ouyang, Yingjia Wan, Ying Nian Wu, Zhijiang Guo, Oscar Leong
papers.summary: A training-free discrete-flow sampler freezes low-entropy positions to prevent correct intermediate predictions from being corrupted later.
papers.use: A transferable decoding idea for discrete hypotheses and graph paths.
papers.steal: Measure correct-to-wrong reversals and ablate confidence-based freezing.
papers.doubt: Could overconfident OOD errors be frozen too early?

papers.title: Concept Drift from a Causal Perspective
papers.authors: Eduardo V. L. Barboza, Jean Paul Barddal, Robert Sabourin, Rafael M. O. Cruz
papers.summary: An SCM taxonomy separates drift in exogenous variables, mechanisms, confounders and target generation, with controlled stream generators.
papers.use: Useful for decomposing preclinical-to-patient transfer failures.
papers.steal: Inject distinct causal drift types and compare metric sensitivity and performance loss.
papers.doubt: Real biomedical shifts mix unknown mechanisms; can drift type be identified?

papers.title: Targeted Review for AI-Assisted Biodiversity Surveys: Active Continuous-Score Occupancy Modeling
papers.authors: Timm Haucke, Lauren Harrell, Justin Kay, Mary Clapp, Sara Beery
papers.summary: ACORN allocates expert review to labels most informative for downstream ecological inference rather than classifier accuracy.
papers.use: A strong outside-domain transfer for human review in scientific AI.
papers.steal: Prioritize review by expected impact on the final scientific conclusion.
papers.doubt: Can review utility be defined for open-ended, multi-objective research agents?

papers.title: Task- and dataset-specific information in protein language models
papers.authors: Roman Joeres, Ilya Senatorov, Anastasia Kolchina, Dietrich Klakow, Olga V. Kalinina
papers.summary: Across 13 protein language models and 15 tasks, final-layer embeddings are rarely universally best; a tool selects and truncates at task-specific layers.
papers.use: A direct falsification test for PerturbRx's fixed scFoundation representation.
papers.steal: Probe every scFoundation layer under identical folds and heads for source and patient tasks.
papers.doubt: Will the PLM finding transfer to single-cell models without validation overfitting?

papers.title: WILSON - a pathology foundation model framework for patient-level analysis and diagnostic text generation
papers.authors: Saghir Alfasly, Wataru Uegami, Sobhan Hemati, Wenchao Han, Xiaojia Tang, Kevin Thompson, Daniel Stone, Ghazal Alabtah, Saba Yasir, Michael R. Lucas, Eric W. Klee, Cheryl L. Willman, Judy C. Boughey, Matthew P. Goetz, Krishna R. Kalari, H.R. Tizhoosh
papers.summary: Represents multi-slide, multi-magnification patient cases as composite images and trains a pathology vision-language model on about 189k slides.
papers.use: Relevant as a patient-level multimodal representation design, though not treatment response.
papers.steal: Make the patient case, not the tile or slide, the learning unit.
papers.doubt: Does the advantage survive external site, scanner and rare-cancer shifts?
